subject: SableLytics private deployment: sustained 504s, throughput plateau — ops + exec sync
messages:
From: Amira Patel <amira@sablelytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kenji Ito <k.ito@edgegrid.co>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production problems — private VPC hitting 504s and flat throughput

Hi Jonas / Marissa —

We started seeing sustained 504s and a hard throughput plateau on our private VPC deployment starting ~2027-07-13 18:30 UTC. Error rate shot from ~0.3% to 6.1% on p95 requests; latency p95 jumped from 180ms to 1.4s. End-users are reporting timeouts from our product (search and inline generation).

Attached are: svc_logs_2027-07-14.tar.gz (rotated logs, truncated) and a quick KPI snapshot (sablelytics_kpi_snapshot_2027-07-14.csv). A few excerpts from the logs: 

[2027-07-14T02:41:12Z] auth: request id=acb12... upstream:504 cluster: inference-gpu-2
[2027-07-14T02:41:13Z] runtime: kv-cache miss, stream reset, retry
[2027-07-14T02:43:01Z] worker-7: queue-depth=64 cpu=92% mem=78% cntx-switch=high

We rolled no application changes. On our side we see a recent config change in Redwood: model variant quantized-ggml:v7 was promoted as default on 2027-07-13 17:55 UTC — could that be related? We need this triaged with priority P0 and an executive-facing summary ASAP — our CPO is asking for root cause and mitigation plan in the next 6 hours.

Can you confirm you have someone on this and what immediate mitigation you recommend? We are open to rolling back to the prior model variant or taking a short canary window.

Thanks,
Amira
Head of Platform — SableLytics

---
Attachments: svc_logs_2027-07-14.tar.gz (tar.gz, 8.2MB), sablelytics_kpi_snapshot_2027-07-14.csv (csv, 45KB)

To: Amira Patel <amira@sablelytics.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production problems — private VPC hitting 504s and flat throughput

Amira — thank you for the data and the heads up. I'm pulling an on-call + CS + runtime lead immediately.

Quick notes / asks so we can triage fast:
- Can you confirm whether the infra deploy had any kernel/runtime patches at 2027-07-13 17:00–18:00 UTC?
- Do you have an ingress timeout config that would map to the 504s (we need the timeout value and whether the load balancer is internal)?
- Any spike in request size or seq length distribution?

Initial hypotheses:
1) Runtime kernel fallback on quantized variant causing CPU/KV cache thrash.
2) Batch window and continuous-batching backlog leading to head-of-line timeouts.
3) Network egress saturation on the VPC/private interconnect causing upstream 504s.

Immediate plan (P0):
- Rishi to gather node-level traces and runtime counters (kv-cache hit/miss, pending-batches, avg-batch-size).
- Marissa/Monica to coordinate a 30-min on-call collaboration call and give exec-facing note.
- If we see kernel fallback or sustained high CPU tied to the new model variant, propose fallback to the previous non-quantized variant as a short-term mitigation.

I'm scheduling a 30-minute call now (link in related links). Will update within 30 minutes with findings.

— Jonas
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Jonas / team — joining now. Quick digest from CS + initial traces (attached runtime_trace_initial.json). Key observations:

- Error pattern: 504s originate at the soft-front proxy layer after 10–15s idle waits; backend runtime shows many preempted/gc-like stalls on worker threads.
- CPU profile: worker threads show repeated slow-paths in the fused attention kernel when sequence length spiked above 1024 for certain requests.
- KV cache: eviction rate increased sharply at 02:40–02:44Z; miss rate correlated with higher tail latency.

Notably: the quantized-ggml:v7 variant introduced a kernel fallback code path for several attention kernels. When kernel vectorization is not available (older driver/runtime combo in customer's VPC host image), we see a much higher CPU per token and more context switches — matches logs.

Short-term mitigation options (ordered):
1) Roll back default model variant to the previous float16 variant (can be done via control plane in ~3–5m and immediately reduces CPU pressure).
2) Increase per-node max_concurrent_streams and reduce continuous_batching.window_ms to shrink batching latency.
3) Apply a per-customer routing rule to fall back to Dedicated (if they have reserved capacity) or route to hosted region temporarily (requires exec signoff).

I've attached runtime_trace_initial.json (2.8MB) with stack samples and a CSV of the KV cache counters.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime_trace_initial.json (application/json, 2.8MB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production problems — private VPC hitting 504s and flat throughput

Marissa / team — quick technical plan and commands I've validated on a staging replica:

1) Rollback model variant (fast):
- API: POST /v1/customers/sablelytics/model-override {"model":"open-llama-13B-fp16-v2"} -> expected impact: immediate drop in worker CPU by ~40% on staging.

2) Runtime config changes (canary first):
- Increase max_concurrent_streams from 32 to 64 per node (reduces queue depth).
- Decrease continuous_batching.window_ms from 75ms -> 25ms for low-latency policy.
- Temporarily set kv_cache_size to 1.5x current to reduce eviction pressure.

Commands (runtime-control CLI):
- runtime-control set --cluster sablelytics-private --param max_concurrent_streams=64
- runtime-control set --cluster sablelytics-private --param continuous_batching_window_ms=25
- runtime-control set --cluster sablelytics-private --param kv_cache_size=1.5

3) Observation: collect these counters for 30 minutes post-change: pending_batches, avg_batch_size, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_count, p95_latency, 5xx_rate.

If rollback reduces CPU/tail-latency, we'll schedule a 1-hour canary followed by a full cut. If network egress is a factor, we will coordinate with Kenji at EdgeGrid.

I'll execute the rollback & a config canary in the next 20 minutes pending approval from Jonas for a short canary window (no customer-visible downtime expected; we'll monitor closely).

— Rishi
Senior Runtime Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: ACTION: Canary rollback + runtime canary for SableLytics private deployment — exec note

Amira / team — brief exec summary and ask: we confirmed correlated symptoms between the quantized-ggml:v7 promotion and the spike in CPU and KV eviction on SableLytics' private hosts. Root-cause hypothesis: kernel fallback (quantized variant) + older host driver/runtime in customer's VPC -> higher CPU and KV churn -> queueing -> front-proxy 504s.

Immediate actions (approved):
- 17:55 EDT: Rollback default model variant to open-llama-13B-fp16-v2 (canary, 10% traffic) for 30 minutes.
- 18:10 EDT: If canary shows p95 < 400ms and 5xx < 1%, expand to 100% over 20 minutes.
- Rishi will execute runtime config tweaks if canary does not produce sufficient improvement.

Customer-facing commit: we will run the canary and share a 1-paragraph RCA + mitigation plan within 3 hours. If improved, we'll propose a post-mortem and a driver/runtime compatibility matrix so SableLytics can avoid host-image/driver mismatches in future rollouts.

Exec ask: Jonas requests a short approval for potential cross-region routing to hosted fallback if private canary fails — decision authority: Monica (APM & Enterprise Ops). Monica, please confirm.

Thanks team — I will post the canary telemetry and update the ticket (INF-1123).

— Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
